newsitem.title: GERMANY: Ruehe says no more cuts in German defence budget.
newsitem.headline: Ruehe says no more cuts in German defence budget.

text.p: German Defence Minister Volker Ruehe said on Wednesday there was no more leeway in his budget for Bonn to make cuts to bring its deficit into line to meet the Maastricht criteria for Europe's single currency.
Ruehe told journalists he was already committed to cutting an extra two billion marks from his budget this year. "The savings in the armed forces have reached the end," he said.
Finance Minister Theo Waigel has already said he would seek more budget savings if the spring tax revenue estimate due out on Thursday shows a serious shortfall in Bonn's intake.

Waigel said on Wednesday he was considering selling some of Bonn's shares in Deutsche Telekom AG ahead of schedule to cut the government's borrowing needs before the EU's single currency is launched in 1999.
Ruehe last month warned that any further cuts in his budget could undermine Bonn's commitment to the Eurofighter jet aircraft Germany is developing with Britain, Spain and Italy.
Waigel has said Bonn would make a final decision on financing the procurement of the Eurofighter combat jet when it drafts its 1998 budget this summer.

Ruehe had sought an earlier decision by Bonn to commit to buying 180 Eurofighters after he hammered out a total price of 23 billion marks ($13.5 billion) with German partner Daimler-Benz Aerospace AG (DASA), a unit of industrial giant Daimler-Benz AG.
Britain and Spain have already made a commitment to buy their Eurofighters. The project's partners are British Aerospace, Alenia Spa ALEI.RO of Italy and state-owned CASA of Spain.
